assessment.rationale: The spans state that HTTP/1.0 defined GET, HEAD, and POST, and a general-purpose web server must implement at least GET and HEAD, with all other methods (including POST) considered optional by the specification. The spans state the requirement in terms of GET and HEAD, not GET and POST as claimed.
assessment.provenance_note: Wikipedia HTTP article clarifies server requirement as GET and HEAD minimum; POST is optional. The claim requires GET and POST, which differs from the cited text stating GET and HEAD as minimum with POST optional.
limitations: Spans from a single Wikipedia source; does not cover all possible server implementations or standards beyond those documented.

flags.explanation: The cited specification establishes GET and HEAD as the mandatory minimum; POST is not mandated as part of the core requirement.
